One Airline’s Frantic Race to Avoid a Ground-Stop Meltdown

Southwest halted bag checking and parked aircraft, then moved around planes and crews to get flights back to normal

By

For hours, Southwest Airlines LUV 3.25 % increase; up pointing triangle Chief Operating Officer Andrew Watterson was hunkered in a situation room at the carrier’s Dallas headquarters, trying to avoid gridlock at airports and to figure out how to prevent the Federal Aviation Administration’s ground stop Friday from spiraling into an operational meltdown.

A pressing issue: finding places for the mounting numbers of planes on airport tarmacs to park. Airports were warning they were running out of concrete. Inside the situation room, everyone knew they had to unload planes and move them away from gates as quickly as possible to avoid backups that would have left passengers sitting for hours on tarmacs.
